newsitem.title: UK: Willis H1 prompts profit revisions.
newsitem.headline: Willis H1 prompts profit revisions.

text.p: Stiff competition and the impact of a strong pound prompted analysts to rethink profit forecasts for insurance broker Willis Corroon Plc on Tuesday after a downbeat set of results.
One suggested a reduction in forecasts to below last year's 91.6 million stg looked likely and the group may struggle to make it above the 90 million stg mark.
The moves followed an eight million stg drop in first-half profits to 60.2 million stg.
The strong pound wiped 6.6 million stg off the figures but the company gave no indication of a let up in the tough competition that has characterised the market recently.
"It's a horrific market out there. They're having to run extremely fast just to stay still and because of the currency effect they're actually going backwards," said one analyst.
"To meet second half forecasts there's going to have to be a very heavy swing from first half to second."
The second half was likely to benefit from changes in timing of revenues and changes in the businesses where revenues arose, he said, but the fundamentals of the business remained under pressure.
"The main costs are staff and if you start hacking around staff costs you can lose business," said the analyst.

"Willis's chairman John Reeve has been doing all the right things in terms of battening down the hatches and concentrating on the areas where they're better than others... but we can't see anything on the horizon that's going to really improve the bottom line."
Another analyst pointed to the accelerating competition in the U.S. between both brokers and underwriters as a particular concern and a disappointing performance in the UK energy account.

"Coupled with the strength of the pound plus extra expense for building up operations in the U.S. its going to be hard to make the numbers the market has been going for even if there is a pickup in the second half. The risks are all on the downside," he said.
"They have said the benefits of the change programme would come through in the second half but they're difficult to quantify."
